Your 40-trade backtest might just be luck 🎲

Every backtest metric (win rate, expectancy, profit factor) is an estimate from a sample, and small samples are noisy. In our (hypothetical) simulation, a strategy with zero edge looked as good as a profitable one in about 1 of 4 backtests of 20 trades.

New on the blog:
• the 95% range around a win rate at 20, 100 and 1,000 trades
• how often pure luck passes for an edge
• a simple formula for the trades a strategy needs
• why t = 2 is often too low when you test many variants
• why clustered and correlated trades count as fewer bets
